mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 0.5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive two-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their previous 6-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both above previous 6-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their previous 6-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their previous 12-month averages indicates strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and UNRATE both above previous 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and UNRATE are above their 12-month averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its previous 12-month average for four consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which negatively impacts construction and related sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < previous 12-month average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST is below its 12-month average for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between real personal savings (RSAFS) growth and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as increased household savings can translate into future consumption or financial market participation, supporting equity valuations.
failure_condition: No significant positive correlation between monthly changes in RSAFS and S&P 500 5-day forward returns over a 5-year rolling window.
